_meta.description: Disguised leakage: nothing in the column names says 'after the outcome'. status_code is written by the cancellation flow (C2 → 100% churned). engagement_index_v2 separates the classes perfectly (single-feature AUC 1.0) but non-linearly, so Pearson r is only ~0.11 — a correlation threshold misses it. credit_balance is a pro-rata refund credit, > 0 only for churned customers (zeros, not nulls). tenure, last login, support tickets and spend are legitimately predictive (AUC 0.75-0.84) and must not be called leakage.

required_findings.note: Value C2 occurs only for churned customers: a status written by the cancellation itself.
Perfect class separation (AUC 1.0) with low Pearson r: a non-linear leak.
Non-zero only for churned customers: a refund credit issued after cancellation.

forbidden_findings.note: Known before churn; a legitimately strong predictor (AUC ~0.84).
Plan price; unrelated to the outcome.

note_on_max: Three planted leaks plus an identifier note and a few info notes at most.
